Tropical circulation: warm air rises at equator (low pressure, rainforests), descends at 30 degrees (high pressure, deserts).
Apparent deflection of moving air due to Earth's rotation; right in Northern Hemisphere, left in Southern.
Intertropical Convergence Zone where trade winds meet near equator; band of heavy convectional rainfall, migrates seasonally.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Changing Climate — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Changing Climate brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Changing Climate.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which cell brings rainfall to the equator?
options: Hadley
Ferrel
Polar
Walker

mcqs.q: Where does the ITCZ migrate seasonally?
options: Tropics
Poles
Mid-latitudes
30 degrees only

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
Climate change only happens in summer.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
